title: High-yield isolation of pure fetal endothelial colony forming cells and mesenchymal stem cells from the human full-term placenta
protocol: Obtain healthy human full-term placenta via cesarean section.
Transfer the placenta to an autoclaved stainless-steel tray for dissection and processing within an hour immediately after surgery.
Remove any calcified tissue on the placenta using forceps and scissors.
Use forceps and scissors to remove the thin layer of maternal placental decidua (top layer).
Dissect out 50 g of placental villi, enriched with fetal vasculature, using forceps and scissors.
Transfer dissected placental villi onto a petri dish with washing buffer.
Rinse the tissue with washing buffer until blood residue is removed.
Place the disinfected placental tissue in a sterile container for further processing.
Cut villi into smaller pieces using surgical scissors.
Transfer the tissue into a 250 mL conical flask.
Add 75–80 mL of digestion buffer to the flask.
Digest the tissue for 2 h at 37°C in an incubated, sterile shaker at 65 rpm.
Filter the cell suspension using a 100 μm cell strainer.
Collect the single-cell suspension into 50 mL falcon tubes at approximately 20 mL/tube.
Discard undigested tissue.
Dilute the single-cell suspension by adding 20 mL of ice-cold DPBS per tube.
Pellet the cell suspension via centrifugation using 350 × g with break speed 5 for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard 30–35 mL of the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 30 mL of RBC lysis buffer per 50 mL falcon tube.
Incubate the suspension for 10 min on ice at 4°C.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 350 × g (break speed 5) for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard 35 mL of the supernatant using a 25 mL serological pipette.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 35 mL ice-cold MACS buffer per 50 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge the suspension at 350 × g (break speed 5) for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant using a 25 mL serological pipette.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 20 mL ice-cold MACS buffer.
Resuspend cell pellet at 1–5 million cells per mL of cryopreserving solution.
Quickly aliquot 1 mL of the cell suspension per cryovial.
Place cryovials into a Cool Cell™ Freezing Container and transfer to a −80°C freezer or liquid nitrogen after 24 h.
Add an appropriate amount of pre-warmed (37°C) Complete Culture Medium to a single cryovial of frozen cells.
Gently pipette up and down until thawed.
Transfer the thawed cell suspension to a 15- or 50-mL falcon tube.
Top up each falcon tube to 20 mL with Complete Culture Medium.
Wash the cells via centrifugation at 350 × g (break speed 5) for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant using a 25 mL serological pipette.
Resuspend the soft cell pellet slowly to avoid loss of sample.
Resuspend the cells in 20 mL ice-cold MACS buffer.
Perform a cell count.
Consolidate samples if appropriate, resuspending each pellet in ice-cold MACS buffer at 1 × 10^7 cells/mL.
Set aside a 100 μL aliquot of placental cell suspension (approximately 1 × 10^6 cells) into a sterile 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and keep on ice for flow cytometry with FACS antibody staining controls.
Use Dynabeads™ CD45 depletion to remove hematopoietic lineage contamination, resulting in the CD45NEG cell fraction.
Prime 1 × 15 mL falcon tube of Dynabeads™ CD45 per 2.5 mL of placental cell suspension or less.
Place 250 μL of Dynabeads™ CD45 in 3 mL of MACS buffer and homogenize.
Slot the Dynabeads™ CD45 suspension into the DynaMag™-15 Magnet for 1 min to wash.
Tip the magnet forward, keeping the falcon tube secure, collect, and discard the supernatant.
Remove the falcon tube containing primed Dynabeads™ CD45 from the magnet and resuspend in 250 μL of MACS buffer.
Add 2.5 mL of placental cell suspension (1 × 10^7 cells/mL) to the washed Dynabeads™ CD45 suspension, mix well, and incubate on a roller at 4°C for 20 min.
Incubation complete; add 10 mL of MACS buffer to the Dynabeads™ CD45 cell suspension and place into the DynaMag™-15 Magnet for 2 min.
Collect non-bound CD45NEG cells in suspension by tipping the magnet forward as previously described.
Label collection tubes clearly and adhere to the protocol to avoid collecting the wrong fraction.
Pellet the CD45NEG cell suspension at 350 × g (break speed 5) for 5 min at 4°C to collect the cell pellet.
Carefully remove the supernatant using a 10 mL stripette.
Consolidate CD45NEG samples from separate falcon tubes at 1 × 10^7 cells/mL in ice-cold MACS buffer.
Mix well and incubate on ice for 20 min at 4°C after adding 100 μL of CD34 microbeads to the CD45NEG cell suspension.
Top up the CD45NEG cell suspension with 10 mL MACS buffer following incubation.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 350 × g for 5 min (break speed 5) at 4°C to collect the cell pellet.
Carefully remove the supernatant using a 10 mL stripette.
Resuspend the CD45NEG cell pellet in 5 mL of autoMACS running buffer.
Label two 15 mL falcon tubes as "CD34 negative" (CD34NEG) and "CD34POS" for fraction collection.
Pre-chill tubes by placing on ice for transport to the Miltenyi AutoMACS Pro Separator.
Transport the sample, AutoMACS buffer, and chilled collection tubes to the Miltenyi AutoMACS Pro Separator.
Switch on the Miltenyi AutoMACS Pro Separator and allow the initialisation program to run.
Prime the Miltenyi AutoMACS Pro Separator.
Place the chill rack onto the autoMACS MiniSampler.
Load the CD45NEG cell suspension, CD34NEG collection tube, and CD34POS collection tube into their corresponding positions.
Under the “Separation” menu, fill in the sample separation template field.
Select the “POSSEL” selection program with a “Rinse” wash cycle between samples if appropriate.
Run the program.
Transfer the CD45NEGCD34POS cell suspension to ice.
Label collection tubes clearly.
Ensure adherence to the protocol closely to avoid collection of the wrong fraction.
Perform correct shutdown functions on the Miltenyi AutoMACS Pro Separator.
Pre-wash the LS column by loading 3 mL of MACS buffer and discard the flow-through.
Ensure the column reservoir is empty before proceeding to the next step.
Load the labeled CD45NEG cell suspension onto the pre-washed column.
Collect the flow-through in a new sterile 15 mL Falcon tube, which is the CD34NEG fraction.
Ensure the column reservoir is empty before proceeding to the next step.
Wash the column with 3 mL of MACS buffer.
Collect and combine this wash with the CD34NEG flow-through.
Repeat washing the column three times in total.
Ensure the column reservoir is empty after each wash.
Remove the column from the MidiMACS™ Separator and place it on a new sterile 50 mL Falcon tube.
Pipette 5 mL of MACS buffer onto the column to flush out the magnetic labeled cells, which is the CD45NEGCD34POS cell suspension.
Save this cell suspension.
Top up the CD45NEGCD34POS cell suspension with 10 mL of ice-cold MACS buffer in a sterile BSC.
Pellet the cell suspension via centrifugation at 350 × g (break speed 5) for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μL of ice-cold MACS buffer.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube labeled "Sample".
Place the tube on ice for FACS antibody staining.
Prepare unstained control by adding 50 μL of ice-cold MACS buffer to an Eppendorf tube.
Label seven Eppendorf tubes as single stains (7AAD, CD45, CD34, and CD31).
Label two additional tubes as fluorescence-minus-one (FMO) controls (7AAD-FMO, CD45-FMO, CD34-FMO, and CD31-FMO).
Dilute the 100 μL antibody control aliquot into 450 μL total volume using ice cold MACS buffer.
Place 50 μL of the diluted antibody control into each of the staining control tubes on ice for a total volume of 100 μL per control.
Add the appropriate volumes of CD45, CD34, and CD31 antibodies to their corresponding tubes.
Homogenize thoroughly.
Incubate on ice at 4°C out of the light for 20 min, on a roller.
Incubation complete.
Remove excess antibody by washing.
Add 1 mL of MACS buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspensions at 350 × g (break speed 5) for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant completely.
Resuspend the pellet with 200 μL of ice-cold MACS buffer in each staining control.
Add 500 μL of ice-cold MACS buffer to the sample.
Filter each cell suspension using a 40 μm cell strainer into a labeled 5 mL FACS tube on ice for transport to a sterile flow cytometry facility.
Prepare sterile 5 mL FACS tubes or 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes filled with 500 μL - 1 mL filtered heat-inactivated FBS, labeled ECFC (CD45NEG CD34POS CD31LO) and MSC (CD45NEG CD34POS CD31NEG).
Use a 100 μm nozzle on the flow cytometer to achieve low pressure (approx. 20 psi).
Run samples at a medium flow rate (<2.0) with an event rate of approximately 1,000 events/second.
Sort cells accurately for isolation of both MSC and ECFC stem cell populations via FACS based on provided sample flow plots.
Use the unstained control and single-stained controls to set up compensation.
Generate a forward scatter area (FSC-A) versus side scatter area (SSC-A) to select the total cell population (P1).
Generate an FSC-A versus forward scatter height (FSC-H) to select for singlets, named P2.
Generate SSC-A versus side scatter height (SSC-H) to confirm selection of singlets, named P3.
Generate 7′AAD PE-Cy5A versus SSC-A and gate on the negative fraction, termed P4.
Generate CD34 PE-A versus CD45 FITC-A and create a gate on the CD45NEGCD31POS population, named P5.
Generate a CD31 BV421-A versus SSC-A dot plot panel to identify the CD31NEG MSC population (P6).
Identify the CD31LO ECFC subset of endothelial cells (P7).
Sort these populations directly into ice-cold filtered heat-inactivated FBS.
Place isolated populations on ice and top up with 3 mL ice cold DPBS once back in a BSC.
Pellet cells via centrifugation at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend cells in warmed (37°C) Complete Culture Medium.
Seed cells onto a type I collagen-coated plate at approximately 1 × 10^4 cells/cm².
Culture cells at 37°C in a sterile primary incubator under standard mammalian conditions.
Allow 48 hours for cells to attach to the plate.
Refresh the Complete Culture Medium by carefully pipetting out the old media without touching the bottom of the well, leaving approximately 10% of the old media.
Pipette new media slowly into the wells, placing the tip against the wall, about 1 cm from the base.
Refresh the Complete Culture Medium on a stringent 24-hour basis for 5 days following attachment.

Continue refreshing the Complete Culture Medium on a 48-hour basis until strong High Proliferative Potential ECFCs (HPP-ECFCs) and MSC colonies have formed, taking between 21–28 days for ECFCs and 7–14 days for MSCs.
Wash cells by removing Complete Culture Medium using a pipette tip resting against the wall of the well, close to the bottom.
Leave 10% of the old media in the well to prevent cells drying out.
Place enough DPBS to cover the well by slow pipetting, placing the pipette tip against the wall, approximately 1 cm from the base.
Remove the DPBS and repeat the wash once more.
Complete the final DPBS wash by removing all DPBS from the well.
Add RT TrypLE to the culture plate, for example, add 100 μL to a single well of a 24-well plate.
Incubate cells in the TrypLE at 37°C for 3-5 min.
Using a microscope, check ECFCs or MSCs have detached and gently tap the vessel if necessary.
Add warm (37°C) Complete Culture Medium to inhibit TrypLE and create a cell suspension.
Gently wash over the bottom of the well with the Complete Culture Medium cell suspension to ensure all cells detach.
Transfer the cell suspension to a sterile 15 mL Falcon tube with an additional 1 mL Complete Culture Medium.
Pellet via centrifugation at 500 × g for 5 min at room temperature and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL warm Complete Culture Medium.
Seed ECFCs into a type I collagen-coated plate of the same size previously used and incubate at 37°C under standard conditions.
For MSCs, graduate to a 12-well plate after cell adhesion.
Allow 48 hours for cells to adhere to their plates.
Replenish media every 24 hours for the first 5 days following adherence.
After the initial 5 days, replenish media every 48 hours.
Repeat passaging to a minimum of P3 before cryopreservation, seeding cells at a density of 1 × 10^5/cm^2 from P1 onwards.
Resuspend cells at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL in cryopreservation solution.
Aliquot 1 mL cryopreservation cell suspension per cryovial.
Place the aliquoted vials into a Cool Cell™ Freezing Container.
Transfer the Cool Cell™ Freezing Container to a -80°C freezer or liquid nitrogen.
